questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Culture, city size, courses and cost of living

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was mostly difficult finding information on courses. You can see courses in their course catalogue, but the date and time are only available once you have arrived and filled in your OLA

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not much, but you're guided on how to check-in via the university e-mail. Would have been nice with an in-person "welcome"-session.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was lucky that previous, Danish students helped me with a WhatsApp number on a landlord.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is very common and no problem at all. The city is quite small and the university campus is scattered all over.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was lucky, but with the big housing shortages, it would be great if University of Bologna took more responsibility since they accept a big number of exchange students - and in my impression, a rising number.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You get an email notifying you on a virtual check-in that must be done upon arrival and then you're guided via zoom by an employee. Worked well.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Do not know what else

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I succeeded in the end, but it wasn't that easy. I had an OLA signed by both parties long before arrival but without knowing the exact timetables and apparently some of them were master courses, which I thought I could take without problems, since they approved it, but it was very insecure whether that was possible once the courses started. We had to argument our way through and many others bachelor students weren't allowed. That would be a good thing to sort out with the university, because it creates a lot of uncertainty.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Trust the process. It is not as well-organized and see-through as KU, but they will help you, once you're there.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of BA courses was lower than here at KU but the master level ones were great in my opinion.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was more in-class with a professor which was nice and it was a bit more inclusive of the students than KU. A little bit less focus on grand theories and more on class discussion and the creation of a space where people wanted to contribute.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Visualizing the Italian Society, Criminology of the Borders, Political Behavior and Institutions & Politics and Policies of the European Union.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Criminology of the borders! The professor, Giulia, is a great teacher whose passion for understanding migration dynamics is big and sets the tone in the classroom. There are many guest lecturers and class discussions, which makes it extremely interesting and worthwhile to attend.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Even though food, coffee etc. is cheaper (on average) in Bologna compared to Copenhagen, I just spent more than I thought I would on going out to eat, drinking coffees etc.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: A little bit more expensive to find housing than I thought.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't attend, unfortunately, but I considered it many times and it seemed very accessible. I joined a running club though, but it wasn't affiliated with the university.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Academic event, CUSB offered a variety of different sports you could attend with student discount

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join a sport!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Take the train somewhere! It's cheap if you buy it well in advance and Trenitalia is so much better than DSB! It's a pleasure and you can travel quickly from north to south. But also! Stay in Bologna and get to know it on the weekends as well, instead of rushing around to all the major cities in Italy.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was interesting, easy and challenging at the same time. I knew Italy quite well in advance, but still, it's something else, when you know it is going to be your home for a few months. But people are nice, curious and welcoming in Bologna and that makes it way easier.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: CUSB (sports) and "Labas" on Wednesdays (hosts events, bars etc. in the center)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their caring for one another, their insistence on not stressing and their very honest expression of emotions

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Clear with the professors that you're allowed to enroll in their course (if master and you are a bachelor student). 

You do not have to stay inside the walls, there are many really nice areas just outside. But be careful when finding a landlord online. I would go see it physically before or make sure that someone you know can vouch for the landlord.

Look forward to it. It is a wonderful city to spend a few months.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not at the moment.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Listening to Italian all day, everyday and having lots of free time to walk around. Aaaaand living with other exchange students form other countries.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Balancing the number of visits, because bologna is "close" to home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
